records.title: Southeastern Saline Everglades annual land-cover classification layers from 1984 to 2024
records.abstract: This dataset comprised annual land-cover classification layers for the Southeastern Saline Everglades from 1984 to 2024 with an 30 m spatial resolution. The classification includes three classes: Degradation Zone (DZ), Transition Zone (TZ), and Vegetation Zone (VZ), representing the typical land covers in the area. For the classification layers, a value of 1 denotes the vegetation zone (mangrove), 2 denotes the degradation zone, and 3 denotes the transition zone. Degradation zone is characterized by dieback of freshwater species with exposed bright soil and sparse mangrove shrubs. Vegetation zone is characterized by dense mangrove canopy that completely covered the soil surfaces. Transition zone features an approximately equal coverage of mangrove and freshwater species, with vegetation density in between of degradation and vegetation zone. Compared with Version 1, this version incorporates harmonized Landsat-5 and Landsat-7 observations adjusted to Landsat-8 equivalent values using Roy's coefficients, improving temporal consistency across the entire time series.

records.title: Sea-level rise and freshwater management are reshaping coastal ecosystems in the Florida Everglades
records.abstract: Datasets include hydrology (water level and salinity), net ecosystem exchange of CO2, photosynthetically active radiation (PAR), and air temperature for a freshwater marl prairie, brackish marsh ecotone, and saline scrub mangrove forest. Data were derived from multiple sources, including two sites from the South Florida Water Management District (SFWMD) DBhydro web database, two sites from the Florida Coastal Everglades Long Term Ecological Research (FCE-LTER) program and three AmeriFlux sites in the Southeastern Everglades region. Ameriflux sites were co-located with FCE-LTER sites. To understand the effects of sea level rise and freshwater management on landscape carbon exchange (C), we measured the net ecosystem exchange of CO2 (NEE) between subtropical wetland ecosystems and the atmosphere along a dynamic salinity gradient. Ecosystems were representative of freshwater marl prairies, brackish marsh ecotones, and saline scrub mangrove forests. In the southeastern Everglades, the magnitude of environmental change was greatest along the coast, where mangrove scrub forests exhibited a greater capacity to maintain CO2 uptake with changing conditions.

records.title: Inventory of Eddy Covariance Tower Data in AmeriFlux from Everglades Towers (2004-ongoing) and Auxiliary Data from SRS-6 Mangrove Forest Tower (2004-2023), Florida, USA
records.abstract: There are six eddy covariance towers that make continuous measurements of regional hydrology and carbon balance in the region. This long-term eddy covariance tower network includes 2008-ongoing data collection in a freshwater marl prairie (TS/Ph-1; US-Esm) and a freshwater marsh (SRS-2; US-Elm), 2016-2021 data collection from a mangrove scrub (TS/Ph-7; US-TaS), 2004-2023 data collection from a tall mangrove forest (SRS-6; US-Skr), 2020-ongoing data collection from a tower at the ecotone of marl prairie and mangrove scrub (SE1; US-EvM), and 2018-ongoing data collection from an aquatic Tower in Florida Bay (Bob Allen Key; US-FBE). This data package is an inventory of eddy covariance tower data and metadata available through the AmeriFlux repository. This package also contains environmental and meteorological variables measured at the SRS-6 mangrove forest using an eddy covariance flux tower in the southeastern Florida Coastal Everglades from 2004 to 2023.

records.title: Benchmark dataset for comparing eddy covariance measurements and gradient flux calculations across 47 National Ecological Observatory Network (NEON) flux towers, August 2021 - August 2026
records.abstract: Gradient-flux (GF) approaches present an important chance to expand ecosystem-atmosphere observations beyond the gases routinely measured using eddy covariance (EC) alone. We developed a dataset to explore when and where gradient-flux approaches work across diverse ecosystems. We utilized standardized observations from 47 terrestrial sites within the National Ecological Observatory Network (NEON) to develop this continental benchmark dataset for evaluating the performance of three GF approaches, the modified Bowen ratio (MBR), aerodynamic (AE), and wind-profile (WP) methods, against co-located EC measurements of CO2 and H2O. This multi-site benchmark dataset comprises EC and GF fluxes by method and sampling height pair, along with corresponding micrometeorological data. Additional data include: storage fluxes, gradient-flux ensembles, site-level canopy complexity and metadata for tower geometry and sensor heights, ustar thresholds, metadata for validation sites, site canopy attributes, site concentration profiles, and site sampling height pairs.

records.title: Gaps in Network Infrastructure limit our understanding of biogenic methane emissions in the United States
records.abstract: Using multidimensional scaling and a cluster analysis, the US was divided into 10 clusters that were distributed across temperature and wetness gradients (2010-2020). We evaluated the distance to the medoid condition within each cluster. This dataset includes the representative analysis for the US, excluding the locations of EC tower sites, which cannot be provided due to privacy concerns for a small subset of towers. Through our analysis using climate, land cover, and location variables, we have identified priority areas to enhance research infrastructure to provide a more complete understanding of the CH4 flux potential of ecosystem types in the US. For EC tower locations, distance to the medoid coverage was lacking for clusters Na, W, and Nb, and currently clusters Na, W, Eb, and Nb are substantially under sampled. All aquatic sites are under sampled within each cluster.

records.title: CO2 Flux and Temperature Data for Estimating Thermal Acclimation in Ecosystem Respiration
records.abstract: We have compiled an extensive dataset of long-term, hourly CO2 flux measurements from 93 global eddy covariance sites to estimate the thermal response strength in nighttime ecosystem respiration. Flux data was sourced from AmeriFlux, FluxNet, and ICOS. The processed data product encompasses five categories. (1) Long-term, directly measured, Ustar-filtered, hourly or subhourly nighttime ecosystem respiration, along with corresponding air temperature, soil temperature, and soil water content at the 93 sites. (2) Long-term gap-filled data, including hourly or subhourly net ecosystem exchange, air temperature, and soil temperature at these sites. (3) Annual topsoil (< 0.1 m) temperature and nighttime ecosystem respiration curves during the growing season, designed for calculating thermal response strength. (4) Estimated thermal response strength across these sites, detailed with geographic, climatic, soil, and vegetation conditions for each site. (5) An R script to calculate thermal response strength using the data product (3).

records.title: Integrating aquatic metabolism and net ecosystem CO2 balance in short- and long-hydroperiod subtropical freshwater wetlands
keywords: Florida Coastal Everglades, Long-Term Ecological Research
records.abstract: How aquatic primary productivity influences the carbon (C) sequestering capacity of wetlands is uncertain. We evaluated the magnitude and variability in aquatic C dynamics and compared them to net ecosystem CO2 exchange (NEE) and ecosystem respiration (Reco) rates within calcareous freshwater wetlands in Everglades National Park that vary in hydroperiod. We continuously recorded 30-minute measurements of dissolved oxygen (DO), water level, water temperature, and photosynthetically active radiation (PAR). These measurements were coupled with ecosystem CO2 fluxes over 5 years (2012-2016) in a long-hydroperiod peat-rich, freshwater marsh and a short-hydroperiod, freshwater marl prairie. Daily net aquatic primary productivity (NAPP) rates indicated both wetlands were generally net heterotrophic. Net aquatic primary productivity accounted for 4-5% of the deviance explained in NEE rates.

records.title: Chamber measurements of carbon dioxide (CO2) and methane (CH4) in Everglades following Hurricane Irma: 2017 - 2019
records.abstract: On September 9, 2017, highwinds from Hurricane Irma impacted the Florida Everglades. With 24 hours of heavy rain along with strong winds and storm surge, the storm caused higher than normal water levels, wind-induced defoliation, uprooting of plants and soil disturbance in Everglades short-stature freshwater wetlands. The hurricane redistributed short-stature vegetation into dead mats in Everglades National Park. The high post-storm water levels saturated many of these dead mats, slowing decomposition and increasing their persistence on the landscape. In this study, we measure carbon dioxide (CO2) and methane (CH4) fluxes at dead mats and compared them to the ridge and slough of freshwater marsh and to the marl prairie.

records.title: Fire in the Everglades, 1978-2023
records.abstract: In the Florida Everglades, fire is a key driver of ecological dynamics, interacting with hydrology and vegetation structure. Fires have been recorded by Everglades National Park and Big Cypress National Preserve (1978-2023) by mapping the outer boundary of fires. Annual fire perimeter data for the two regions were combined to generate a fire history database for the subtropical landscape. This dataset includes fire perimeters, binary burned layers, and years of fire layers that can be used to quantify fire dynamics across subtropical ecosystems.

records.title: Fire perimeter files for wildfires and prescribed fires in Everglades National Park 1948-2019
records.abstract: Everglades National Park has an extensive fire program. The park records both prescribed and wildfires by digitizing fires that occur within the park boundaries. Fire perimeters are provided as a shape file that has all known fires that occurred from 1948 to 2019. These perimeters were digitized by park staff to record the outer boundaries of fires. Annual shape files of fires obtained from the park were standardized in R and combined into a single shape file. Although much of the Everglades is inundated throughout different parts of the year, these are fire maintained ecosystems.

records.title: RustMapper: White Pine Blister Rust Risk in the Western United States, 1980-2023
records.abstract: White pine blister rust (WPBR) is a highly destructive disease threatening high-elevation five-needle white pines across North America. To better understand risk patterns, we analyzed data from independent studies conducted across the western U.S. between 1995 and 2020. Using this data, we assessed WPBR risk for high-elevation five-needle pine species (High-5) from 1980 to 2023, integrating the results into the adaptive management tool "RustMapper." These projections estimate the annual probability of WPBR occurrence, providing valuable insights for monitoring and management. Risk ranges from 0 to 1, and values closer to 1 indicate a higher likelihood of disease occurrence based on conditions.

records.title: California drought assessment
records.abstract: This data set was developed using satellite imagery, MODIS (land cover, NPP, GPP, and ET) and PRISM (precipitation and scPDSI) data sets, for the entire state of California from 2002 to 2013. Satellite imagery was re-sampled to match the resolution of the scPDSI data set (4km) using bilinear methods of interpolation and re-projected to UTM WGS84 using the R library raster. To remove effects of possible changes in vegetation classes or errors in classification, cells that did not maintain the same ecosystem class over the study period were masked. This data set contains mean annual estimates for scPDSI, precipitation, leaf area index (LAI), gross primary productivity (GPP), net primary productivity (NPP), carbon uptake efficiency (CUE=GPP/LAI), and water use efficiency (WUE=NPP/ET).
